title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 2 of Grothendieck's letter to Serre of 27 August 1965. The letter is published in the Grothendieck–Serre Correspondence (SMF 2001; AMS bilingual edition 2003). It is the first written formulation of what became the 'standard conjectures'.

Setting: X is smooth, projective and connected of dimension n over an algebraically closed field k. Y is a smooth hyperplane section with class ξ in C^1(X). C^i(X) denotes codimension-i cycles modulo algebraic (τ-)equivalence, tensored with Q.

Conjecture A (previous page): for 2i ≤ n, multiplication by ξ^{n-2i} gives an isomorphism C^i(X) → C^{n-i}(X). This is a hard-Lefschetz statement for cycles. Grothendieck says it suffices to prove surjectivity, and only in the case n = 2i+1. He identifies the first open case as i=1, n=3.

The page first finishes recalling the cohomological weak Lefschetz theorem: the Gysin map H^i(Y) → H^{i+2}(X) is bijective for i ≥ n and surjective for i = n-1. It then states a cycle-theoretic weak-Lefschetz analogue.

Conjecture A': for 2i ≥ n-1, the Gysin map C^i(Y) → C^{i+1}(X) is surjective. Equivalently, every cycle of dimension j < n/2 on X is τ-equivalent to the push-forward of a Q-cycle on Y.

Grothendieck claims, 'sauf erreur', that A' implies A, and that again one may take n = 2i+1. He notes a subtlety: the reduction seems to need A' over non-algebraically-closed base fields, for cycle classes rational over that field. Otherwise one must state A for homological equivalence, losing the 'purely geometric' character he had promised Serre.

He then lists consequences of A:
- the Künneth formula for cycles (he retracts his earlier claim that the two are equivalent);
- hence integrality theorems, e.g. for coefficients of characteristic polynomials, possibly up to powers of p in denominators;
- hence all the Weil conjectures except the absolute values of the eigenvalues (the Riemann hypothesis), which is to come from B;
- A is the 'minimum minimorum' needed for a usable definition of motives over a field.

Conjecture B: for n = 2m, let P^m(X) be the kernel of multiplication by ξ from C^m to C^{m+1}. Then (-1)^m deg(x·x') is positive definite on P^m(X). This is the Hodge-index standard conjecture. Positive semi-definiteness already suffices for Weil. The strong form gives τ-equivalence = numerical equivalence (= ℓ-adic homological equivalence, which lies between them) and finite-dimensionality of the C^m(X).

The next page goes on to finite generation, semisimplicity of motives, Galois semisimplicity, and the restatement A'': C^i(U) = 0 for 2i > n, where U = X − Y is affine.
errors: As stated, for cycles modulo algebraic (τ-)equivalence tensored with Q, Conjectures A and A' are false. Griffiths (1969) showed that on a general quintic threefold, homologically trivial curves need not be algebraically trivial, even rationally. Clemens (1983) showed Griff^2(X)⊗Q can be infinite-dimensional. Then C^2(X) is infinite-dimensional while C^1(X) = NS(X)_Q and C^1(Y) = NS(Y)_Q are finite-dimensional. So multiplication by ξ, and the Gysin map, cannot be surjective in exactly the case n=3, i=1 that Grothendieck singles out as 'le premier cas qui échappe'. The same examples refute A'' for algebraic equivalence.

Likewise, the claimed consequence of B, 'τ-équivalence = équivalence numérique' with C^m(X) finite-dimensional, is false for algebraic equivalence (Griffiths). This is why Grothendieck's 1968 Bombay formulation (published 1969) uses homological/numerical equivalence. His own hesitation here ('ou se borner à énoncer A pour l'équivalence cohomologique') points in that direction.
The reduction A' ⇒ A and the reduction to n = 2i+1 are marked 'sauf erreur' and are not proved here.
Minor: the extra hypothesis that p-power denominators may appear in the integrality results is stated as a possibility, not resolved.

missed.claim: Grothendieck claims a proof (unwritten, 'sauf erreur') that the weak-Lefschetz-type statement A', reduced to n = 2i+1, implies the hard-Lefschetz-type Conjecture A. He notes that the argument requires A' over non-algebraically-closed fields for rational classes. Read for homological equivalence, this reduction of the Lefschetz standard conjecture to Gysin surjectivity for a hyperplane section is a coherent strategy. I am unsure whether a full written proof of 'A' ⇒ A' (with the descent subtlety) exists in the literature.
missed.quote: sauf erreur je sais prouver la conj.A à partir de la forme plus faible suivante (dans la nature d'un théorème de Lefschetz "faible")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Weak-Lefschetz-type statements for algebraic classes on hyperplane sections may be more accessible than hard Lefschetz. The remark about the base field needing to be non-algebraically closed is a specific technical point of the argument. This is published in the Correspondence, so it is not uncredited, just apparently not developed.

deep.surprise_reason: This page is part of a well-known, published letter (Grothendieck–Serre Correspondence) that first states the standard conjectures. Its content is fully credited. The only notable points are the unproved A' ⇒ A reduction and the algebraic-equivalence formulation, which Griffiths and Clemens later showed false.
